h1:
15 Great-Vibe Stays
on Koh Kood, Trat
We Reviewed Them All
heroSub: 15 hand-picked Koh Kood stays we've reviewed in depth — from beachfront white-sand pool villas and Bali-style bungalows on a sea-view hill to clear-water beach resorts and easygoing homestays by the mangroves. Rates from about ฿1,000–18,000/night.
heroStats: ✅ Honest take from real reviews, every one
introH2: 🏝️ What kinds of stays does Koh Kood have, and how do you pick the right one?
introHtml: Koh Kood is Thailand's fourth-largest island, sitting at the far eastern edge of the Gulf of Thailand in Trat province, and it's one of the most unspoiled islands you'll find — clear water, white-sand beaches, forest still green, and crowds nowhere near those on the more famous islands · What makes choosing a stay here different is that "which bay" matters more than the star count — some people pay a premium for a beautiful villa but land on a small, rocky bay, while others pay under two thousand baht and get a Bali-style bungalow on a sea-view hill they'll remember for years · This guide rounds up 15 places to stay on Koh Kood that we've already reviewed in depth, across every budget and style — luxury pool villas on Klong Chao Beach, beachfront resorts on Bang Bao and Ao Tapao bays, bungalows on the hill, and easygoing homestays · Every one comes from reading real guest reviews, telling you both the upsides and the honest caveats, with a 3-site price check and direct booking links throughout
mrtHtml: Koh Kood has no major roads or public transport — getting around the island runs mostly on resort shuttles or rented motorbikes · From Bangkok it's about a 5–6 hour drive to Laem Sok pier or the Koh Kood pier in Trat province, then another 1–1.5 hours by ferry or speedboat · The main accommodation bays in this guide: Klong Chao Beach — the longest, prettiest white-sand beach and the one closest to the village of restaurants, good for anyone who wants to walk out and eat off-resort · Bang Bao Bay — a curved bay with clear water, snorkeling right off the beach · Ao Tapao — quiet, with a private beach, good for proper relaxing · Ao Ngamkho · Klong Mad · Ao Phrao · Ao Yai Ki — small, quiet bays scattered around the island, most of which need a vehicle to get anywhere easily

entries.type: Luxury Pool Villa Resort, 5-Star · every room has a private pool
entries.name: High Season Pool Villa & Spa Koh Kood
entries.badge: 🏊 Most luxe pool villas · every room has a pool
tags: 🏊 42 villas, every room with a private pool
🌅 Sunset views on the west coast
entries.addr: 117 Moo 2, Klong Chao Beach, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: If you want the most luxurious pool villas on Koh Kood where every room genuinely has its own pool, High Season Pool Villa & Spa is the name many reviews bring up first — a 5-star resort on Klong Chao Beach with 42 villas, from a 95 sqm Deluxe up to a 180 sqm Beachfront Suite closest to the sand, and a Trip.com score of 9.3 from about 807 reviews, which is a lot for an island stay · What guests agree on most is the private white-sand, clear, shallow-water beach in front of the resort, which many families say is safe enough for kids to splash around in, and the west-coast sunset that's pretty enough to become an evening ritual · Beyond the in-villa pools there's kayaking, yoga classes, a dive service, and a four-treatment-room High Spa with sauna and steam that earns praise for its service · Reviews say the staff are warm and the atmosphere uncrowded, a fit for couples and families who want a genuinely private villa stay · Honest caveats to know before you book: getting to Koh Kood is far harder than reaching Koh Chang — you'll spend about 1–1.5 hours on a boat with high car-and-boat costs, food and drinks at the resort cost more than outside, and it sits away from the village, so heading out to off-resort eateries isn't as easy as from the middle of Klong Chao Beach · There are also reports the resort is set to close for renovation for about two months in mid-2026, so always check the open/closed dates and boat schedules before booking · Bottom line: if the budget's there and you want the most complete beachfront pool villa on Koh Kood, this is the number-one pick in this guide
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want sea views and to be closest to the beach, go straight for the Beachfront Suite Pool Villa · Book a package with breakfast included and budget a bit high per meal since the resort restaurant is pricey · And check with the resort about the mid-2026 renovation closure and boat schedules before booking
pros: Every room is a true pool villa with a private pool — 42 of them, from 95 to 180 sqm
Private white-sand, clear, shallow-water beach, safe for kids (per reviews)
High Spa plus kayaking, yoga and diving all on offer, with warm service
West-coast sunset views, uncrowded atmosphere
cons: Far to reach — a 1–1.5 hour boat transfer and high car-and-boat costs
High food and drink prices at the resort · sits away from the village
Reported to be closing for renovation for about 2 months in mid-2026 — check before booking

entries.type: Beach Resort, 4-Star · pool villas + beach villas
entries.name: The Beach Natural Resort
tags: 🏡 A mix of villas in nature
entries.addr: Bang Bao Bay, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: The Beach Natural Resort is a resort whose name tells you exactly what it's about — a focus on nature along Bang Bao Bay, a curved, clear-water bay on the south side of Koh Kood · What guests mention in nearly every review is the private wooden pier reaching out over the sea, which has become a favorite photo spot and a memorable place to watch the sunset · The water off Bang Bao Bay is so clear that paddling out on the free kayaks the resort provides, you don't have to go far to find coral and schools of fish for snorkeling · There's a range of rooms by budget, from a Bali-style Natural Cottage in the garden about 50–80 m from the beach, up a notch to a Crescent Cottage on the hill with a bay view, to a Beach Villa on the sea and a two-bedroom pool villa for families · Reviews praise the breakfast and the friendly-but-polished service, a fit for anyone wanting a beachfront stay with a quiet, close-to-nature feel · Honest caveats to understand before booking: the beach in front of the resort is fairly narrow and rocky in places, so if you're hoping for a wide white-sand beach to stroll along, it may not match the picture — the selling point is clear water more than a long beach · Food and drink at the resort run about 10–40% higher than outside, and finding eateries on the island is tough, so choose a breakfast-included package and budget extra · Some rooms are starting to show their age and have few power outlets, so go for the renovated beach villa or pool villa, check the latest room photos before booking, and bring a power strip just in case · Bottom line: it suits nature lovers who value clear water and quiet over a wide sandy beach
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Grab a beach lounger early since there are limited numbers · Go for a renovated room type like a beach villa or pool villa and check the latest photos before booking · Choose a breakfast-included package and bring some snacks and water since the resort restaurant is pricey
pros: Bang Bao Bay's water is very clear — paddle out on free kayaks to snorkel coral and fish
A private wooden pier and sunset views that guests mention in every review
A mix of villas in nature, from affordable cottages to a beach villa on the sea
Good breakfast, friendly-but-polished service
cons: The beach in front of the resort is fairly narrow and rocky in places
Food prices at the resort run about 10–40% higher than outside
Some rooms are starting to age and have few power outlets (per reviews)

entries.type: Beachfront Resort, 2-Star · garden bungalows by the beach
entries.name: Dusita Resort Kohkood
entries.badge: 🌟 Highest score in this guide · budget-friendly
tags: 🛵 Mid-island location, easy to get around
entries.addr: Ao Ngamkho Beach, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Don't write off Dusita Resort Kohkood just because it's only a 2-star place, because this is the stay with the highest score in this guide at 9.7 from about 150 reviews on Trip.com — a number that tells you just how impressed real guests are · What pushes the score this high isn't luxury, it's the atmosphere and the care · Fan and air-con bungalows are dotted across a shady, well-kept garden and lawn so neat that many reviews call it the best-maintained stay on Ao Ngamkho · The owner and staff are the heart of the place — guests consistently describe them as warm and friendly, looking after you like family — and the beachfront restaurant is tasty and affordable, with breakfast made fresh to order · It sits right in the middle of the island, and many people use it as a base to rent a scooter and ride out to swim at Klong Chao Beach and the island's sights, which is great value starting at only about ฿4,500/night · It's best for couples and travelers who want a simple, warm garden bungalow with good food and no big price tag · Honest caveats to know: Ao Ngamkho isn't the prettiest beach on the island — parts are coarse sand and the shallows are rocky, so you can't fully enjoy a swim right in front, and you'll want to ride over to Klong Chao or another nice beach instead · The rooms keep it simple, bungalow-style rather than luxury villas, with no big pool, so pick an air-con room if you want to stay cool · And there's a review warning about pricing on some platforms, so compare a few sites or message the resort directly to confirm before booking · Bottom line: it's one of the best value-for-score, value-for-money stays on Koh Kood
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Use Dusita as a mid-island base, then rent a scooter to ride to Klong Chao and other nice beaches · Pick an air-con room if you want to stay cool · And compare a few platforms or message the resort directly to confirm the price before booking, choosing a free-cancellation rate
pros: 9.7 — the highest score in this guide, from about 150 real reviews
Warm, friendly owner and staff who look after you like family
Neat, well-kept garden bungalows; breakfast made fresh to order, tasty and affordable
Mid-island location, handy as a base to explore the island, with friendly starting rates
cons: Parts of Ao Ngamkho are coarse sand with rocky shallows — not the prettiest beach
Simple bungalows with no big pool — not luxury villas
A review warns about pricing on some platforms — compare and confirm before booking

entries.name: Tinkerbell Privacy Resort
entries.badge: 💑 Open your door onto the beach · small, quiet resort

rooms.type: Beach Front Villa (open the door onto the beach)

tags: 🏖️ The far end of Klong Chao Beach
🚪 Open your villa door onto the beach
entries.addr: 116 Moo 2, Baan Klong Chao, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Tinkerbell Privacy Resort sits at the far end of Klong Chao Beach, one of the prettiest beaches on Koh Kood — fine white sand, clear water, and a sunset right in front of the beach · The selling point really is in the name "Privacy," because there are only 15 villas, making the atmosphere very quiet and private, and guests say the staff look after you warmly, like they know every guest · The highlight couples love most is the Beach Front Villa, where you fold open the doors and walk straight onto the beach, while the Pool Villa is a two-story villa with a private pool and a hammock on the upper balcony · The resort has free kayaks, and crucially it's in the Klong Chao area with restaurants and cafés within walking distance off-resort, so you don't have to eat in every meal · It's best for couples and anyone wanting a small, quiet resort on a pretty beach, with the beach right outside the door and attentive service · Honest caveats to understand before booking: this place has been open since 2009, leaning into a natural, beachside feel rather than new-build luxury — some rooms show wear and damp in the rainy season, so ask for a recently renovated villa and check the latest room photos before booking · Breakfast options are limited and restaurant prices are fairly high for the quality, so make the most of the Klong Chao location and walk out to eat off-resort · And if you come in the rainy season (May–Oct), check the opening dates and boat schedules with the resort first, since many island places close or scale back · Bottom line: it's worth it for those who value the beach and privacy over new-build luxury
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want the open-the-door-onto-the-beach experience, go for the Beach Front Villa · Ask for a recently renovated villa and check the latest room photos before booking · Make the most of the Klong Chao location and walk out to eat off-resort to save, and check the opening dates and boat schedules if you come in the rainy season
pros: At the far end of Klong Chao Beach, one of the island's prettiest beaches — white sand, clear water
Beach Front Villa opens onto the beach · two-story Pool Villa with a private pool
A small resort of just 15 villas — genuinely quiet and private, with staff who know their guests
Free kayaks · restaurants and cafés within walking distance off-resort
cons: Open since 2009, nature-focused — some rooms show wear and damp in the rainy season
Limited breakfast options · restaurant prices fairly high
In the rainy season many island places close or scale back — check opening dates and boat schedules first

entries.type: Bali-Style Beach Resort, 3-Star · Bali bungalows on a hill
entries.name: Koh Kood Beach Resort
entries.badge: 🌅 Bali bungalows + a sea-view infinity pool
tags: 🏡 Bali bungalows on a sea-view hill
entries.addr: 121 Moo 1, Klong Mad, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Koh Kood Beach Resort is a clear example of why the star count isn't everything on Koh Kood — a 3-star resort with a 9.5 on Trip.com and one of the best-vibe stays in this guide · It's about 19 thatched-roof Bali bungalows lined up on a lawn that slopes down toward the sea in the Klong Mad area, with both garden and sea views, and open-air bathrooms that suit the island-resort feel · What guests remember most is the infinity pool on the hill looking out over open sea as far as the eye can see — both a photo spot and a place to sit and watch a sunset that many reviews say is unforgettable · Below the hill there's a small private bay, with free kayaks and bicycles, good food, warm staff, and the Klong Mad pier just about 170 m away for easy coming and going · It's best for couples and families who want a quiet bungalow on a sea-view hill with a lovely pool, at a price more attainable than luxury villas — starting at only about ฿2,400/night · Honest caveats to know: the beach in front is small and rocky in spots, not great for a long swim, so use the infinity pool as your main spot and ride a motorbike to swim at Ao Tapao about 10 minutes away · The Klong Mad area is quiet, with restaurants and shops a roughly 15-minute drive away, so plan to eat mostly at the resort or keep a rented motorbike on hand · And the open-air bathrooms of the Bali Houses come with the island's natural insects and geckos, so bring your own mosquito repellent · Bottom line: it's great value in Koh Kood's mid-price range
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Use the hilltop infinity pool as your spot to swim and watch the sunset, then ride a motorbike to swim at Ao Tapao about 10 minutes away · Pick a sea-view Bali House or the Sunset House if you want the full view, and bring your own mosquito repellent since the bathrooms are open-air
pros: Bali bungalows on a sea-view hill, quiet atmosphere, high 9.5 score
Sea-view infinity pool and a sunset guests remember most
A private bay, free kayaks and bikes, good food, warm staff
From about ฿2,400, more attainable than luxury villas · near Klong Mad pier
cons: The beach in front is small and rocky in spots — not great for a long swim
The quiet Klong Mad area — restaurants are a roughly 15-minute drive away
Open-air bathrooms come with the island's natural insects and geckos

entries.type: Beachfront Resort, 3-Star · beachfront bungalows at the canal mouth
entries.name: Peter Pan Resort
entries.badge: 🏖️ On Klong Chao Beach + free kayaks
tags: 🏖️ On Klong Chao Beach, at the canal mouth
🔥 Evening fire show on the beach
entries.addr: 102 Moo 2, Baan Klong Chao, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Peter Pan Resort sits in a really interesting spot on Klong Chao Beach — right at the canal mouth where Klong Chao flows out to the sea, giving you both sea and canal views in one place, white sand, clear water, and a sunset right in front of the beach · It's about 48 beachfront bungalows in several styles and price points, from the most affordable garden-view Mermaid up to the Sea Horse by the pool with a sea view · What guests like is the activities and the freebies — free kayaks to paddle into Klong Chao, free ice cream and drinks at times, an evening fire show on the beach, and reviews praising staff who are good with kids, a fit for families · It's in the Klong Chao area, with restaurants and cafés off-resort within walking or scooter distance, so you don't have to eat in every meal · It suits couples and families who want a pretty beachfront bungalow with activities, at a price more attainable than luxury villas · Honest caveats to know before booking: some rooms and beds could use an update — many reviews mention hard or sagging mattresses, bathrooms with odors and old plumbing, and some linens with stains, so check the latest room photos and pick a recently renovated unit · Music from the bar runs loud until late and disturbs nearby rooms, so if you're a light sleeper, ask for a room away from the bar and pack earplugs · Breakfast options are limited, and if you come in the rainy season, check the opening dates and boat schedules first · Bottom line: choose your room carefully and it's great value for a pretty beach on a friendly budget
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Check the latest room photos and pick a recently renovated unit, since some mattresses are hard/sagging · Ask for a room away from the bar and pack earplugs just in case, since the music runs loud until late · Use the free kayaks to paddle into Klong Chao and catch the evening fire show on the beach
pros: Right at the Klong Chao canal mouth — both sea and canal views, white sand, clear water
Free kayaks into the canal · freebies at times · evening fire show on the beach
Staff good with kids, a fit for families · prices more attainable than luxury villas
In the Klong Chao area, with restaurants off-resort within walking/scooter distance
cons: Some rooms and beds could use an update · some bathrooms have old plumbing (per reviews)
Music from the bar runs loud until late and disturbs nearby rooms
Limited breakfast options · check opening dates and boat schedules first in the rainy season

entries.type: Beachfront Eco Resort, 3-Star · bungalows on Ao Tapao beach
entries.name: Medee Resort
entries.badge: 📣 Most reviews in this guide · quiet private beach
tags: 🏖️ On the private Ao Tapao beach
entries.storyHtml: Medee Resort is the stay with the most reviews in this guide at about 541, scoring 8.7 on Trip.com — a number that tells you it draws a lot of guests and has a loyal fan base · The main selling point is bungalows right on the private Ao Tapao beach, where you can walk from the bungalow to the sand in a few steps, the beach is quiet with almost no one around, and the west side gets a pretty sunset · The style here is an eco-resort that leans into unfussy nature, bungalows in a green garden, a calm atmosphere good for relaxing and slowing down · There are free kayaks to paddle along the bay, plus snorkeling and dive trips to the islands around, and reviews praise the breakfast · It's best for anyone wanting a quiet, private beachfront stay on Koh Kood at an attainable budget, starting at only about ฿2,960/night · Honest caveats to know before booking: there's no pool here — the focus is swimming in the sea in front instead — so if your trip needs a pool for kids or you like a soak, consider a place with a pool · Ao Tapao is away from the main restaurant area and some of the nicer beaches, so without a motorbike you'll spend most of your time at the resort and eating there — keep a rented vehicle on hand · And garden-view rooms don't see the sea from the room, so if you want a sea view from your room, request a Beachfront or Sea View at booking since they're limited and sell out fast · Bottom line: it's great value for anyone set on a quiet beachfront stay, not after a pool or nightlife
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want a sea view from your room, request a Beachfront or Sea View Cottage at booking since they're limited and sell out fast · Keep a rented motorbike on hand to ride out to other beaches and restaurants, since Ao Tapao is quiet and has no pool
pros: The most reviews in this guide, about 541, with a loyal fan base
On the private Ao Tapao beach — a few steps to the sand, quiet with almost no one around
Eco style, nature-focused, calm atmosphere, breakfast earns praise
Free kayaks and water activities · from about ฿2,960, attainable
cons: No pool — the focus is swimming in the sea in front instead
Ao Tapao is away from the main restaurant area — tough to get out without a vehicle
Garden-view rooms don't see the sea — request a Beachfront/Sea View, but they're limited

entries.type: Beach Resort, 3-Star · beachfront bungalows on Bang Bao Bay
entries.name: Koh Kood Resort
entries.badge: 🐠 Snorkeling in front of the resort · budget price
tags: 🐠 Snorkeling in front of the resort
🌊 A curved bay with clear water
entries.addr: 45 Moo 5, Bang Bao Bay, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Koh Kood Resort is a beachfront resort on Bang Bao Bay that sells value above all — beachfront bungalows on Koh Kood starting at only about ฿2,500/night, which counts as easy to reach for a beachside stay · Bang Bao Bay is a crescent-shaped sandy beach sloping into water so clear you can see the sandy bottom, and what guests like most is being able to snorkel right in front of the resort — there's coral and schools of fish to see without taking a boat out · There's a beachside pool, a restaurant that earns praise, and a beach bar with a pretty sunset view · Bungalows come in several styles, from the budget Garden View up to a Sea View Bungalow looking out over Bang Bao Bay from the balcony · It suits anyone wanting a beachfront Koh Kood stay with clear water and snorkeling, at a price that isn't high · Honest caveats to know before booking — this is what pulls the 8.2 below others in the group: some bungalows are starting to age, with hard or sagging mattresses, damp, and maintenance that could be better, so pick a sea-view or newer room type and check the latest room photos and reviews before booking · Some nights the beach bar plays music or has a DJ until late, so if you sleep light, choose a room far from the bar or check with the resort about which nights have music · And when it's busy the staff can be stretched thin and service slow at times, so allow extra time and accept that it's a small-island resort focused on an easygoing vibe more than speed · Bottom line: choose your room well and it's worth it for clear water on a budget
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a sea-view or newer room type and check the latest room photos and reviews before booking, since some units are aging · Choose a room far from the beach bar or check with the resort about which nights have music if you sleep light · Be ready to snorkel right in front of the resort since the water is clear with coral
pros: Snorkel right in front of the resort, with coral and schools of fish
Bang Bao Bay is a curved bay with clear water, pretty sunset view at the beach bar
A beachside pool, a restaurant that earns praise
A beachfront Koh Kood stay from about ฿2,500, easy to reach
cons: Some bungalows are aging, with hard/sagging mattresses; maintenance could be better
Some nights the beach bar plays music/has a DJ until late
Service can be slow at times when it's busy (per reviews)

entries.type: Hillside Villa Resort, 4-Star · hilltop villas with sea views
entries.name: Shantaa Koh Kood

rooms.type: Shantaa Extra Sweet (up to 3 guests, sea view)
Shantaa Extra Sweet PLUS (up to 4 guests)

tags: 🌄 Hilltop villas on 35 rai, few guests
entries.storyHtml: Shantaa Koh Kood is a resort that genuinely sells quiet and wide-open space — villas spread through the forest on a hill above Ao Tapao on a plot of about 35 rai, which keeps guest numbers low and the feel private, and many rooms see the sea from up high, with open-air bathrooms · It scores 9.4 from about 385 reviews on Trip.com, reflecting consistent satisfaction · What guests agree on in praise is the fresh breakfast and good coffee, the sea-view restaurant, the Ghati café, the seaside bar, and the infinity pool looking out over the sea · It's been family-run since 2004, takes few guests, and local staff look after you warmly, like they know their guests, with free kayaks and surfboards · It's best for couples and anyone wanting a quiet resort on a sea-view hill, wide space with few guests, and a grown-up atmosphere · Honest caveats to know before booking: the beach in front is a small rocky one, not a wide white-sand beach you open the door onto — if a sandy beach is the main thing, consider a resort on Klong Chao Beach instead, or use Shantaa as a quiet base and drive to sandy beaches elsewhere · The villas are on a hill, so you'll walk up and down ramps and stairs between the rooms, pool, and restaurant — if you're coming with elderly travelers or several small kids, tell the resort to request a room on an easier-to-reach level · And some room types are compact for the price · If you come in the rainy season, check the opening dates and boat schedules first · Bottom line: it's worth it for those who value quiet, the view, and private space over a wide sandy beach
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If walking is tough or you're with elderly travelers, tell the resort at booking to request the easiest-to-reach level · Use Shantaa as a quiet base and drive to sandy beaches elsewhere, since the beach in front is rocky · Don't miss the breakfast and the Ghati café that guests praise
pros: Hilltop villas in 35 rai of forest, few guests, private, many with sea views
Good breakfast, the Ghati café, a seaside bar, and a sea-view infinity pool
Family-run since 2004, with warm local staff
Free kayaks and surfboards · quiet, a fit for couples
cons: The beach in front is a small rocky one, not a wide sandy beach
The villas are on a hill — you'll walk up and down ramps and stairs
Some room types are compact for the price (per reviews)

entries.type: Beach Bungalow Resort, 3-Star · sea-view bungalows on a headland
entries.name: Horizon Resort Koh Kood
tags: 🌅 Panoramic sea views on a headland
entries.storyHtml: Horizon Resort Koh Kood is a stay that sells the view above all — bungalows set on a headland between two beaches in the Klong Chao area, so the front-row bungalows and the restaurant get wide panoramic sea views, with a seaside bar for watching the sunset · It's about 20 traditional Thai-style bungalows with private balconies and open-air bathrooms that fit the island feel · There are kayaks and snorkel gear to borrow free with no time limit, and a private clear-water beach a few steps down from the bungalows · It suits anyone coming to Koh Kood for sea views, sunsets, and quiet on an attainable budget, starting at only about ฿2,500/night · Honest caveats to know before booking: this is the lowest-scoring stay in this guide at 7.8, and there are honest reasons — the bungalows are natural-style wood that's starting to age, with low water pressure at times, so if you want a brand-new room and a system that doesn't hiccup, ask for a bungalow in good condition at booking or consider a newer boutique resort in the same area · There's no pool and the beach chairs are limited, the focus being the beach and water activities, so it suits anyone who values the view and the sea over full facilities · And Koh Kood is at the far eastern edge of the Gulf of Thailand, taking several legs of car and boat, so plan your round-trip boat schedule and island transfer in advance, and check that the resort is open for the dates you're going · Bottom line: if you put the view and the price above newness, this is still worth it
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a front-row Horizon Bungalow for the full panoramic sea view, and ask for a bungalow in good condition at booking since some are aging · Use the free kayaks and snorkel gear · Plan your round-trip boat schedule and check the resort is open for the dates you're going
pros: Panoramic sea views on a headland between two beaches, with a seaside sunset bar
Kayaks and snorkel gear to borrow free, no time limit
A private clear-water beach a few steps away · wooden bungalows with open-air bathrooms
Sea views from about ฿2,500, attainable
cons: The bungalows are starting to age, with low water pressure at times
No pool, and limited beach chairs
Koh Kood is far to reach, taking several legs of car and boat — plan ahead

entries.type: Pool Villa Resort, 4-Star · pool villas on a rocky headland
entries.name: Captain Hook Resort
entries.badge: 🏝️ Private rocky headland, 2 beaches + a kayak canal
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Yai Ki · near Klong Rahan · Koh Kood
entries.addr: 15/9 Moo 4, Ao Yai Ki, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Captain Hook Resort is one of the most distinctive stays on Koh Kood — set on a rocky headland jutting into the sea at Ao Yai Ki, near Klong Rahan (Secret Beach), with private white-sand beaches on two sides, quiet as if you had an island of your own · What sets it apart is that you arrive by the resort's longtail boat in about 5 minutes — a charm that cuts you off from the bustle entirely · There's a mangrove canal to paddle a kayak into and explore, plus kayaks, SUP, snorkel gear, and free drinks and ice cream all day · Rooms come in several styles, from a Deluxe Villa up to a Mini Pool Villa and a Pool Suite with a private pool and sea view · Reviews praise staff who look after you so well that people come back, a fit for anyone wanting a quiet private island and water activities · Honest caveats to know before booking: because it's on a headland you reach by longtail boat, heading out each time isn't convenient and there are car-and-boat costs, so it's better for those set on staying mostly in the resort — if you want to tour the island's many beaches, look at a roadside stay that's easier to come and go from · Some rooms are older with a natural feel, so go for a newer Mini Pool Villa or Pool Suite · Breakfast focuses on Thai dishes, and fresh coffee costs extra · And if you come in the rainy season, check the opening dates and boat schedules first · Bottom line: it suits anyone who wants to cut off from the world and values nature over easy access
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Plan to come and go as few times as possible since it's a longtail-boat trip with car-and-boat costs — set yourself up to stay mostly in the resort · Go for a newer Mini Pool Villa or Pool Suite with a private pool · Make the most of the free kayaks into the mangrove canal and the free activities
pros: A private rocky headland with white-sand beaches on two sides, quiet as if you had your own island
A mangrove canal to kayak · kayaks, SUP, snorkel gear, and freebies all day
Mini Pool Villa and Pool Suite with a private pool and sea view
Staff who look after you so well that people come back (per reviews)
cons: You arrive by longtail boat — heading out isn't convenient and there are car-and-boat costs
Some rooms are older · breakfast focuses on Thai dishes, fresh coffee costs extra
In the rainy season many island places close or scale back — check opening dates and boat schedules first

entries.type: Beachfront Bungalow Resort, 3-Star · beachfront bungalows on a quiet bay
entries.name: A-Na-Lay Resort Koh Kood
entries.badge: 🐠 Snorkel under the pier to see fish · from ฿1,000
tags: 🐠 Snorkel under the pier to see fish
entries.addr: Klong Chao Beach area (the resort's own private bay), Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: A-Na-Lay Resort Koh Kood is a stay whose clear strength is its reachable price — fan rooms starting at only about ฿1,000/night, which counts as very cheap for a seaside stay on Koh Kood, up to a beachfront sea-view room with a jacuzzi at about ฿4,000 · It sits in its own bay on the west side near Klong Chao, with a quiet, private atmosphere · What guests call the highlight is the snorkeling spot under the pier in front of the resort, where the water is clear with plenty of fish — you can see them without taking a boat out — and the Sea View and Jacuzzi bungalows on the sea where you can sit and watch the sunset from the balcony · It suits anyone wanting a beachfront stay on a quiet Koh Kood bay at a reachable budget, with a clear-water snorkeling spot · Honest caveats to know before booking: reviews are fairly mixed, and the quality and upkeep of the bungalows vary by section — this place has been open since 2005, with older rooms in some parts dealing with damp and age, while the beachfront section and the parts renovated in 2024 are clearly better, so pick a beachfront or renovated bungalow and request it at booking; if you want genuine new-build luxury, consider a higher-tier resort on the island · The resort is in its own bay away from the Klong Chao area, with limited food options on-site, so keep a rented scooter on hand to ride out to eat and plan dinner ahead · And in the rainy season the water can turn murky, making snorkeling less good, so check the opening dates and boat schedules first · Bottom line: it's worth it on a tight budget if you choose your room well
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a beachfront or 2024-renovated bungalow and request it at booking, since room quality varies by section · Don't miss the snorkeling under the pier in front of the resort · Keep a rented scooter on hand to ride out to eat, since it's away from the Klong Chao area
pros: Reachable prices — fan rooms from about ฿1,000 to beachfront rooms around ฿4,000
A snorkeling spot under the pier in front, clear water with plenty of fish, no boat needed
Sea View and Jacuzzi bungalows on the sea with sunset views
A quiet private bay, a fit for anyone wanting calm
cons: Mixed reviews, room quality varies by section, some older rooms have damp
In its own bay away from the Klong Chao area, with limited food options
In the rainy season the water can turn murky, snorkeling less good — check opening dates and boat schedules first

entries.name: Koh Kood Paradise Beach
entries.badge: 🏖️ 200 m private beach + a photogenic orange pool
tags: 🛶 Kayaks and snorkeling off the beach
entries.storyHtml: Koh Kood Paradise Beach is a resort on Tapao Beach that sells privacy and a long beach — the white-sand beach in front runs about 200 meters, clear and shallow, good for a quiet stroll along the sea morning and evening with few people around · What guests photograph most is the eye-catching orange pool that pops against the blue of the sea, a popular check-in spot, with a separate kids' pool for families · There are kayaks and snorkeling to see coral near shore, plus a beach bar, a seaside massage spa, and a motorbike rental at about 300 baht/day · Rooms come in several styles, from a Superior Room from about ฿2,200 up to a Deluxe Beach Front Villa and a sea-view Deluxe Pool Suite · It suits anyone wanting to relax on a private beach on Koh Kood at an attainable budget · Honest caveats to know before booking: food prices at the resort are higher than on the mainland and heading out to eat isn't convenient, so budget extra or rent a motorbike to ride out and try local spots · Service standards aren't always consistent in some periods, since it's an island resort where everything moves at an easygoing pace — if you're after polished luxury at every turn and nightlife, it may not fit your style · And some budget rooms are aging, so to make the trip out to Koh Kood worth it, step up to the villa group or a sea-view/Beach Front room at booking · Bottom line: it's worth it for a long private beach on a mid budget, if you choose your room and set your expectations right
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: To make the long trip worth it, step up to the villa group or a sea-view/Beach Front room at booking, since some budget rooms are aging · Budget extra for food or rent a motorbike at about 300 baht/day to ride out and try local spots · Don't miss photographing the orange seaside pool
pros: A private white-sand beach about 200 meters long, clear and shallow, quiet with few people
A photogenic orange seaside pool, plus a separate kids' pool for families
Kayaks and snorkeling off the beach, a beach bar, a seaside massage spa
Several room styles, from about ฿2,200 up to a sea-view pool suite
cons: Food prices at the resort are higher than on the mainland, heading out to eat isn't convenient
Service standards aren't always consistent in some periods (per reviews)
Some budget rooms are aging

entries.type: Homestay / Guesthouse · near Klong Chao Waterfall
entries.name: Dara Homestay
entries.badge: 💰 Most budget-friendly · warm owner, tasty breakfast
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mid-island, near Klong Chao Waterfall · Koh Kood
tags: 🌊 Near the waterfall and Klong Chao Beach
entries.addr: 37/10 Moo 1, Ko Kut, Ko Kut District, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Dara Homestay is the pick for anyone wanting to do Koh Kood as cheaply as possible — a homestay of about 15 rooms in the middle of the island, near Klong Chao Waterfall and Klong Chao Beach, starting at only about ฿1,300/night including breakfast, which is among the cheapest on the island · The biggest strength that real reviews agree on is the owner-made breakfast, made fresh, good-tasting, and better than the price you pay · The owner and staff are warm and friendly, the rooms are clean and quiet, and there's a vehicle-and-bike rental and a mini-mart on-site, handy as a base to head out and explore the island in every direction · It's best for budget travelers who want a clean place with lovely owners and a tasty breakfast, then use it as a base to head out · Honest caveats to understand before booking: this place isn't on the beach — it's in the middle of the island, so you'll need a vehicle or to walk/ride to swim at Klong Chao Beach or the waterfall; if you want to step from your room onto the beach, consider a beachfront resort at a higher budget instead · It's a small homestay with no pool, no spa/gym, using the nearby Klong Chao beach and waterfall instead · And Koh Kood has no public transport, so staying mid-island is tough without a vehicle — rent a motorbike through the property, or pick a beachfront stay you can walk around from if you'd rather not drive · Bottom line: it's the best value on Koh Kood for anyone who doesn't need to be on the beach and has a vehicle
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Rent a motorbike through the property from day one, since mid-island has no public transport and isn't on the beach · Use this as a base to ride to swim at Klong Chao Beach and the nearby waterfall · Don't miss the owner-made breakfast that reviews praise as the biggest highlight
pros: Owner-made breakfast, made fresh, better than the price — the biggest highlight
From about ฿1,300/night including breakfast, among the cheapest on the island
Warm owner and staff, clean and quiet rooms
A mid-island base, near the waterfall and Klong Chao Beach, with vehicle rental and a mini-mart
cons: Not on the beach, mid-island — you need a vehicle or to ride to swim
A small homestay with no pool, no spa/gym
Koh Kood has no public transport — staying mid-island is tough without a vehicle

entries.type: Artsy Homestay by the mangroves · just a few rooms
entries.name: Gumm Lonely Club
entries.badge: 🎨 Artsy by the mangroves · hosts look after you like family
tags: 👵 Hosts look after you like family
entries.addr: 63/2 Moo 5, Ao Phrao Beach, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Gumm Lonely Club is a stay unlike any other in this guide — a small artsy homestay renovated from a fisherman's house by the mangroves in the Ao Phrao area on the south side of the island, with just a few rooms and a score as high as 9.6 on Trip.com · What impresses guests isn't luxury, it's the sincerity — the hosts are Khun Gumm and Khun Jaeng, who welcome you warmly and help with everything, and real reviews mention them with appreciation almost across the board, like staying at a relative's home · The Thai food is Khun Jaeng's handiwork, made fresh on every plate, with the menu adjusted to dietary restrictions (give 2–3 hours' notice for dinner) · You can paddle a kayak out from in front of the place into the quiet mangroves, and it's about a 5-minute walk to the white sand of Ao Phrao · It's best for anyone wanting a Koh Kood experience that's sincere, quiet, and friendly on an attainable budget · Honest caveats to understand before booking: this is a small homestay with no pool, no room service, and simple, house-like facilities — if you want full-hotel convenience, consider a larger resort on the Ao Tapao or Klong Chao side instead · Wi-Fi and phone signal in the Ao Phrao zone aren't always strong, so if you need the internet to work, bring a SIM with good signal or see it as a chance to take a break from screens · And it often asks for a multi-night minimum stay and sits toward the south of the island, suiting trips set on staying a while and living slowly rather than passing through · Bottom line: it's a stay that sells charm and sincerity, not luxury
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Order Khun Jaeng's homemade dinner by giving 2–3 hours' notice, and you can name any dietary restrictions · Bring a SIM with good signal since Wi-Fi in the Ao Phrao zone isn't always strong · Plan to stay several nights since it often asks for a minimum, and kayak through the mangroves in front of the place
pros: Hosts Khun Gumm and Khun Jaeng look after you like family, reviews appreciative almost across the board, 9.6 score
Homemade Thai food by the hosts, made fresh, with the menu adjusted to restrictions
Artsy decor by the mangroves, kayak through the mangroves in front of the place
About a 5-minute walk to the white sand of Ao Phrao · from about ฿1,800/night
cons: A small homestay with no pool, no room service, simple facilities
Wi-Fi and phone signal in the Ao Phrao zone aren't always strong
Often asks for a multi-night minimum stay, sits toward the south of the island

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates from the standard room range and may change by date and season — we recommend checking the real price and comparing 3 sites before every booking · The scores and highlights in this guide come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms, not from staying ourselves · Koh Kood is an island where nature is still intact, reached by ferry or speedboat from a pier in Trat province in about 1–1.5 hours, and there's no public transport on the island, so most people use resort shuttles or rent a motorbike · In the rainy season (May–Oct) many resorts and shops on the island close or scale back and boats run less often, so always check the opening dates and boat schedules with your stay before booking, and choose a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't firm · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travelers ask most about Koh Kood stays

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best place to stay on Koh Kood?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style and budget · By review score, Dusita Resort at 9.7 is the highest in this guide despite being a budget-friendly 2-star bungalow, with Gumm Lonely Club at 9.6 · If you want the most luxurious pool villas, High Season Pool Villa & Spa has a pool in every room · By number of reviews, Medee Resort has the most at about 541 · For couples wanting a small, quiet resort, Tinkerbell or Shantaa · On a tight budget, A-Na-Lay from ฿1,000 or Dara Homestay ฿1,300

faq.q: ❓ How much do Koh Kood stays cost?
faq.a: In this guide, prices start at about ฿1,000–18,000 per night · On the budget side it's A-Na-Lay from ฿1,000, Dara Homestay ฿1,300, and Gumm Lonely Club ฿1,800 · The mid range is beachfront bungalows and resorts at about ฿2,200–4,500 (Koh Kood Beach Resort, Koh Kood Paradise Beach, Medee, Dusita, Shantaa) · And the top tier is pool villas like High Season from ฿9,250 (up to about ฿18,000 for the beachfront room) · All prices are approximate starting rates from standard rooms, and during festivals and high season they can run higher than usual

faq.q: ❓ Which bay is best to stay on Koh Kood?
faq.a: Klong Chao Beach is the prettiest white-sand beach and the one closest to the village of restaurants, good for anyone who wants to walk out and eat off-resort (High Season, Tinkerbell, Peter Pan) · Bang Bao Bay has clear water with snorkeling right off the beach (The Beach Natural, Koh Kood Resort) · Ao Tapao is quiet with a private beach, good for proper relaxing (Medee, Shantaa) · Ao Ngamkho, Klong Mad, Ao Phrao, Ao Yai Ki, and mid-island are quieter but mostly need a vehicle to get anywhere easily (Dusita, Koh Kood Beach Resort, Gumm, Captain Hook, Dara)

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Koh Kood, and how long does it take?
faq.a: From Bangkok, drive or take a bus to a pier in Trat province (such as Laem Sok pier or the Koh Kood pier) in about 5–6 hours, then continue by ferry or speedboat for another 1–1.5 hours · Koh Kood is considerably farther than Koh Chang, and there's no public transport on the island — most people use resort shuttles or rent a motorbike · Book your round-trip boat schedule and island transfer in advance, and check that your stay is open for the dates you're going

faq.q: ❓ When's the best time to visit Koh Kood · is it open in the rainy season?
faq.a: The best window is November–April, with clear seas, good weather, and resorts and shops all open · In the rainy season (May–Oct), many resorts and shops on the island close or scale back, boats run less often, and the sea can turn murky · If you're going in the rainy season, always check the opening dates and boat schedules with your stay before booking, and choose a free-cancellation rate · Some resorts like High Season are reported to be closing for renovation for about two months in mid-2026, so check first

faq.q: ❓ Which Koh Kood stays suit families and tight budgets?
faq.a: For families, Koh Kood Paradise Beach has a 200-meter private beach and a separate kids' pool · Peter Pan Resort gets reviews praising staff who are good with kids · High Season Pool Villa has a shallow-water beach safe for kids · On a tight budget, A-Na-Lay Resort from ฿1,000 on the sea, Dara Homestay ฿1,300 mid-island with a tasty breakfast, and Koh Kood Beach Resort ฿2,400, Bali bungalows on a sea-view hill

Honest take from real reviews, real scores, rates from about ฿1,000–18,000/night, price-checked across 3 sites with direct booking links.
